method.metaDescription: A 15-step engineering workflow that teaches students to think systematically before writing code — from problem analysis to real product delivery.

hero.title: The 15-Step Engineer Method
hero.subtitle: We replicate the real-world workflow of professional software engineers, streamlined and adapted to match the thinking of students aged 6 to 17.

overview.lead: Every problem — simple or complex — goes through these 4 stages.
overview.step1Desc: Start from a real-life situation or challenge.
overview.step2Desc: Analyze input, output, conditions, logic, parameters, events, objects…
overview.step3Desc: Design pseudocode, flowchart, algorithms and solution architecture.
overview.step4Desc: Build a real product to solve the problem — no copying, no shortcuts.

steps.heading: 15 implementation steps
steps.subheading: Every step can be applied to any programming language.

why.heading: Why does this process matter?
why.card1Body: Most beginners jump straight into writing code. This workflow forces students to fully understand the problem before writing the very first line of code.
why.card2Body: Skills like pseudocode and flowcharting are language-agnostic. This is the core thinking that follows an engineer throughout their entire career.

about.metaTitle: About IQode Lab · Our Story & Team
about.metaDescription: IQode Lab is an edu-tech startup teaching computational thinking to kids 6–17. We build logical thinking and problem-solving skills, not just syntax.

hero.title: About IQode Lab
hero.subtitle: We believe learning to code isn't about making every child a developer. It's the best way to train Logical Thinking and Problem-Solving Skills — skills that survive the AI era.

story.heading: An edtech startup born from genuine passion
story.body1: IQode Lab was founded by software engineers with a burning question: why do most Vietnamese students learn programming but still can't solve simple real-world problems?
story.body2: The answer: because we teach language, not thinking. IQode Lab was created to change that.

pillars.heading: 4 Pillars of Educational Philosophy
pillars.p1Desc: Apply logical thinking to solve real-world problems. Every challenge is solvable when you reason in the right direction.
pillars.p2Desc: Break problems down — define each phase — map solutions. The skill to split large problems into manageable parts.
pillars.p3Desc: Build the habit of self-study, self-debug, and self-improvement — no waiting. The most important skill in a rapidly evolving industry.
pillars.p4Desc: Every skill is aimed at creating real products and value. Students don't just know theory — they build things that work.

team.heading: Academic Team
team.m1Bio: Former Software Engineer at Big Tech. Deeply believes in hands-on, practitioner-led teaching.
team.m2Bio: Master's in Computer Science, STEM product specialist.
team.m3Bio: AI Researcher passionate about inspiring the next generation.
team.m4Bio: Specialist in early childhood technology education.
